clue.text: Value seen in still back and neck

indicators.note: the value is seen inside the other word, so one piece sits within another
the word for still is read backwards, as the clue says it comes back

parts.note: still, as in 'yet', means YET
value or worth is MERIT

explanation.surface: Someone appraising a figure that is motionless from its back to its neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for still, and 'seen in' puts the value inside. 'Neck' is the informal sense of cheek, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck in its slang sense is brazen cheek or audacity, the same rash boldness.

clue.text: Index to the French pictures

parts.note: an index, as in a list of contents, is a TABLE
AUX is French for 'to the' before a plural

explanation.surface: A guide to French paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableaux are striking scenes or living pictures, a plural noun like the definition.

clue.text: Great man is coming, if a suitable arrangement can be made

indicators.note: the clue invites a suitable rearrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: An important visitor is arriving, provided suitable plans are made.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging COMINGIFA gives the answer; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico is a Venetian grandee, hence any person of high rank or importance.

clue.text: Wander about having hurried up, say

parts.note: hurried, as in rushed, is RAN

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: say, as in for example, is EG

explanation.surface: Someone strolls around after rushing upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the abbreviation; 'having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To range is to roam freely over an area, so to rove.

clue.text: No metal went into this classical pillar

indicators.note: the letters go into a new form, rebuilt as the column

explanation.surface: A Greek column made with no metal at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A telamon is a column carved as a male figure; the female version is a caryatid.
explanation.definitionFit: A telamon is a column in the shape of a man, used in classical architecture.

clue.text: I give no answer: I am all over the place

parts.note: a quiz contestant who cannot answer says 'pass'
I am contracts to I'M

explanation.surface: A flustered quiz contestant admits being unable to answer and feeling scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Latin word used in footnotes for a reference found throughout a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin for 'here and there', used of a term occurring throughout a text.

clue.text: Spot wild bear about in one continent

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the other word
wild suggests the letters are scattered in disorder

parts.note: a spot or mark is a STAIN

explanation.surface: Seeing a wild bear roaming in a continent such as North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles BEAR to ABER and 'about' wraps it round the spot. 'Continent' is the adjective meaning self-restrained, not a landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from drink or indulgence is self-restrained, the adjective's moral sense.

clue.text: No copper used inside plug for basin

indicators.note: used inside means the leftover letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: to plug a hole is to STOP it

indicators.note: No drops the C from the chemical symbol, leaving the last letter

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A sink plug with no copper in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper's symbol CU, with 'No' dropping the C, leaves U, which goes inside STOP: STO-U-P.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoup is a stone basin for holy water in a church.

clue.text: Result of this insect's being winged?

definitions.text: Result of this insect's being winged?

parts.words: Result of this insect's being winged?
parts.note: the insect's name, split in two, hints that having wings means it might possibly take to the air

explanation.surface: A biology question about what happens when an insect grows wings.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the insect's name reads 'may fly': with wings it is able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: This short-lived insect with delicate wings has a name that also means 'is permitted to take off'.

clue.text: To do with abnormal growth of Caesar's wars?

explanation.surface: A question about a tumour connected with Caesar's campaigns.
explanation.walkthrough: A gall is an abnormal growth on a plant; Caesar wrote of his Gallic Wars in Gaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic can relate to plant galls (as in gallic acid) and also means of Gaul, Caesar's conquest.

clue.text: Battle perhaps traps private in open

indicators.note: one word traps the other, holding it inside

parts.note: Ben Battle is the soldier in Thomas Hood's comic ballad 'Faithless Nelly Gray', so Battle's first name gives BEN
a private soldier, in American usage a GI

explanation.surface: A battle catches an ordinary soldier exposed in open ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle perhaps' asks for a man whose surname is Battle: Hood's Ben Battle. 'Open' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to start or commence it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Splash the principal floor

parts.note: principal, as in main or chief, is LEAD
a floor of a building is a storey, here in the spelling also used in America

explanation.surface: Someone splashing water about on the main floor of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splash' is newspaper slang for the big front-page item, not a spill of water.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a splash is the most prominent article on the front page, the top item of the day.

clue.text: Skinny mare plied furiously

indicators.note: working furiously suggests the letters are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: A thin horse is worked hard and furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' reads as thin, but here it means 'of the skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidermal means relating to the outer layer of the body's covering, so skinny in a literal sense.

clue.text: Horrify a returning Northerner

indicators.note: returning means the word for the northerner is read backwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a native of Lapland in the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A traveller from the north comes back home and shocks people.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with dismay or shock, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A sinister arms supporter, the beast

explanation.surface: An ill-omened gun-runner is described as a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry 'sinister' is the left-hand side (as the bearer sees it) and the supporters are the creatures holding up a shield; on the British royal arms the lion stands on the right, the single-horned beast on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-horned mythical horse supports the royal coat of arms on its left side, and is also a fabled creature.

clue.text: Only half the story credited

indicators.note: half keeps the first two of the four letters of only

parts.note: a story or narrative is an ACCOUNT

explanation.surface: Only part of the tale was believed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credited' means put on the slate, bought on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying something on account means it is charged to one's credit and paid later.

clue.text: Savoury taken out of tin to copy

parts.note: a tin is a CAN
to copy or mimic is to APE

explanation.surface: A savoury snack is lifted out of a tin to be imitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savoury' is a noun: a small savoury morsel on bread or pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small savoury morsel on a biscuit or toast, served with drinks.

clue.text: Men hope an assembly will produce remarkable people

indicators.note: an assembly puts the letters together in a new order

explanation.surface: Men expect a gathering to produce outstanding individuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are prodigies, extraordinary persons, the plural of a word for a marvel.

clue.text: Deranged Trollope's heiress loses her head

indicators.note: losing her head means the name drops its first letter

parts.note: Miss Dunstable is the rich ointment heiress in Anthony Trollope's 'Doctor Thorne' and 'Framley Parsonage'

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel's heiress goes mad and is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Martha Dunstable, rich from the 'Ointment of Lebanon', loses her D.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstable means mentally unbalanced, close to deranged.

clue.text: Element Finn may find in Lett?

explanation.surface: Someone from Finland may discover a chemical element in a Latvian.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as CO-BALT: a Lett (Latvian) is a Balt, and a Finn, from another Baltic state, might see him as a fellow Balt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a metallic chemical element, number 27, and split up it suggests a fellow Baltic native.

clue.text: Out East, type of lily is the flower of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: out means the letter for East is removed

parts.note: the tiger lily is a type of lily
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: In the Orient, a lily species is the bloom of ancient Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword word for a river, something that flows. Removing E from TIGER leaves TIGR.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is a thing that flows, so a river, and this one runs through Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Cutter to race along

parts.note: to race forward is to SURGE
to go along is to go ON

explanation.surface: A small boat used for cutting through water rushes onward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a boat or a tool; here it is someone who cuts people open in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical specialist who operates is jocularly called a cutter.

clue.text: Feeble-sounding trickery

indicators.note: sounding tells us to say the word aloud and write a word that matches in speech

parts.note: feeble, as in flimsy, is SLIGHT

explanation.surface: A weak-voiced con trick.
explanation.walkthrough: As in sleight of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterous deception, as in a conjuror's sleight of hand.

clue.text: Tastes punishment

explanation.surface: Sampling a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: To smack of something is to taste of it; smacks are slaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that smacks of garlic has its flavour, and slaps on the bottom are a punishment.

clue.text: Wine master at first rejected special terminology

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of master
rejected means the word for special terminology is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: a code is a special system of words or signals

explanation.surface: A head teacher at first dismisses technical jargon about wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses the word for terminology. Médoc is a Bordeaux district on the left bank of the Gironde.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux from the district of that name, a claret.

clue.text: Was girl ill-brought-up? Yes

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Was girl ill-brought-up? Yes (5)' for DELTA: no parse found that builds DELTA from these words, and searches of the exact clue text found no explanation

clue.text: Top dressing in the field

parts.note: top dressing sounds like fertiliser spread on a field, but it means an outer garment worn on top by soldiers in the field

explanation.surface: Fertiliser spread over the surface of a farmer's field.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardeners top-dress soil; here 'top' is an overcoat and 'the field' is the field of battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy military overcoat is outerwear worn over everything else by troops on campaign.

clue.text: There's something characteristic about Welsh accent

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a tang is a distinctive characteristic flavour

explanation.surface: Something distinctive about the Welsh way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: TANG wraps round W to give T-W-ANG; 'There's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality in speech, a regional voice.

clue.text: Showing embarrassment at childish occupation

explanation.surface: A child blushes at being caught playing at some infantile pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is filling in a picture book with crayons.
explanation.definitionFit: Going red in the face shows embarrassment, and filling in pictures with crayons is a children's pastime.

clue.text: A Balkan heard to be short tempered

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are spoken aloud and we write what we hear

parts.note: a Serb is a native of Serbia in the Balkans

explanation.surface: A man from south-east Europe is overheard being irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a Serb' gives the same sounds as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb means sharp and sour in manner, hence irritable or testy.

clue.text: Cabin reserved for worker's occupation

indicators.note: occupation here means the worker takes up residence inside the other word

parts.note: reserved, as in reticent, is SHY
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A hut set aside for a labourer to live in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' looks like a job but is a container signal: the worker occupies the word for reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude hut or shack, the same as a rough cabin.

clue.text: The way a relative may fail to progress?

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
an agnate is a relative on the father's side

explanation.surface: A family member's path may lead nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: AGNATE is a kinsman through the male line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay still and not develop, so to stall without moving forward.
